findings.reason: the fixture description must name at least one runtime source path on the integration branch, or the control silently degenerates to a single path-set assertion and the runtime-classification regression goes unmeasured.
findings.text: the fixture's integration branch "carries many unrelated files" with no runtime source among them, while the first negative control asserts that restoring the two-dot call "fails the test on the path set and on the runtime classification"; with the run's own delta being a test and an evidence fragment, a two-dot range over an integration branch of only non-runtime files still classifies `changes_runtime_source` False, so that half of the control holds on both arms

findings.reason: the section names the rule in words and one grep for `rev-list` in that file finds it, so a worker is not sent to wrong code; the same offset is also written as a precise `node.py:1575` in the cited evidence note, so it is worth correcting when the section is next edited.
findings.text: "this is the rule `reckon/crew/node.py` already applies to commits (near line 1575)" does not resolve: line 1575 falls inside `repository_identity`'s docstring, the rule's function `unintegrated_claim_work` is defined at reckon/crew/node.py:1621, and the `git rev-list HEAD ^<integration_ref> ^<base_sha>` call is at reckon/crew/node.py:1662

findings.reason: the section would otherwise introduce a silent one-way degradation in a caller it names without stating the fallback or asserting it, and the no-remote fixture variant it adds checks only `own_changed_paths` and the carry-forward, so that degradation passes §3's own gate.
findings.text: §3 makes `_changed_figure_paths` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:966) call the new helper, and specifies that the helper returns `None` when the integration ref cannot be resolved, but states the `None` consequence only for `review_head_move` ("no review is carried forward", which is accurate at recovery_review_dispatch.py:1092 where `{}` falls through to a full compose); `_changed_figure_paths` turns `None` into an empty list at recovery_review_dispatch.py:972-973, so after the change a checkout whose primary-branch remote-tracking ref does not resolve dispatches no figure review at all, where today its `base_sha..head` two-dot diff needs no integration ref and does dispatch one

rubric_items.naming: pass — `own_changed_paths` and the retained `changed_paths` name the mechanism, `tests/test_a_review_reads_only_its_runs_changes.py` follows the repository's descriptive test-file convention, and no ticket number, stage label or changelog prose reaches a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section states what `review_head_move` does when the integration ref cannot be resolved but leaves the second caller it changes, `_changed_figure_paths`, unstated, where the same `None` becomes a silent loss of every figure review.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (the `own_changed_paths` helper), its two call sites and one test file; the four assertions all measure the single behaviour the section names.
